entries.triageNote: Accepted by design (route: sUSDe/USDe). The strategy anchors swap minOut to ERC4626 NAV (convertToShares/convertToAssets) rather than an oracle or signed price, a deliberate trust-minimization choice. Review confirmed there is no oracle-free, single-transaction way to detect a skewed pool — the obvious get_dy execution-time cross-check is circular (it reads the reserves an attacker would have just skewed) — so the alternatives (oracle distortion, signer compromise) trade a bounded, quantifiable leak for unbounded trust assumptions. We accept the residual. Residual risk (retained, bounded): up to slippageToleranceBps × tradeSize per swap; economically marginal on the deep sUSDe/USDe pair at normal trade-size-to-depth, growing with looser tolerance, thinner pools, depeg windows, or large swaps relative to depth; bounded because sUSDe NAV is not atomically manipulable (cannot escalate to theft on this route). Compensating control to carry upstream: slippageToleranceBps has no upper bound and defaults to 0 — add a require-enforced hard ceiling + sane nonzero default; operationally keep tolerance near organic slippage and consider private orderflow for large rebalances. Forward-looking: do not deploy this strategy over an ERC4626 whose share price is atomically manipulable — there the NAV reference becomes attacker-controlled and the same code path is a High-severity theft primitive. The merged ex-M-03 last-withdrawer amplification does not apply: clients are owner-curated (setClient onlyOwner), not mutually-distrusting; the requested-not-received decrement is documented-intentional protocol-owned yield. Triaged 2026-05-27. | 2026-06-09: Rejected as false-positive. The use of convertToShares/convertToAssets is intentional — the design allows in-block swaps without MEV fear precisely because the AMM pool is concentrated liquidity. A small slippage tolerance covers 99% of deposit/withdrawal scenarios. The NAV reference is not exploitably skewed in this pool topology. No valid attack path.

entries.note: Dispute upheld (review-finding ryv7m4). Core claim is false: report asserts the recipient absorbs the ENTIRE trade slippage over a (1-f) principal => effectiveBps = slippageBps/(1-f). But _distributeBuffer computes buf = underlyingReceived * bufferShares[i]/totalShares off the ACTUAL post-swap proceeds, so clients get f*underlyingReceived and recipient gets (1-f)*underlyingReceived — both scaled by the same (1-s). Slippage is shared strictly proportionally; the recipient's loss vs its own entitlement is exactly slippageBps for all f. entries.suppressionReason: 'Speculation on future code without a demonstrated root cause' TESTED and REJECTED. The rule's operative words are WITHOUT A DEMONSTRATED ROOT CAUSE. The declaration exists today at IYieldStrategy.sol:79; the four implementers exist today at their own HEADs; and the consequence is mechanically determined (a non-abstract contract missing an interface member does not compile). Only the DATE is future (the next submodule bump), not the mechanism.
